aspects.says: A Callable wrapped in a FutureTask and run on a thread hands its result, or its failure as the cause of an ExecutionException, to whoever calls get().
basis: section:A Runnable Has No Way Back: Return a Result or a Failure Through a Callable

aspects.says: The JVM exits when the last started non-daemon thread ends; daemon threads are then abandoned mid-step, with no exception and no finally.
basis: section:A Daemon Thread Doesn't Hold the JVM Open, and Exit Drops It Mid-Step

aspects.says: setDaemon on a live thread throws IllegalThreadStateException.
basis: section:A Daemon Thread Doesn't Hold the JVM Open, and Exit Drops It Mid-Step
aspects.reason: a rule the JDK enforces with an exception: no wrong solution gets past it, so there is nothing for a plant to break; the page shows the run

aspects.says: A platform thread not told otherwise inherits the daemon status of the thread that creates it, so code that creates threads for work that must finish sets daemon status explicitly.
basis: section:A Daemon Thread Doesn't Hold the JVM Open, and Exit Drops It Mid-Step

aspects.says: Threads are named where they are created, by the constructor, a builder's counter or a ThreadFactory; generated names and unnamed virtual threads make thread dumps unreadable.
basis: section:Name Every Thread Where You Create It

aspects.says: An exception that ends a Runnable's thread goes to that thread's uncaught-exception handler; the starter's join() returns normally.
basis: section:A Runnable Has No Way Back: Return a Result or a Failure Through a Callable

aspects.says: A Thread subclass run by a pool executes on the pool's thread, while its inherited getName() and isInterrupted() describe the never-started Thread object; a task asks Thread.currentThread().
basis: section:A Thread Runs a Task: Write the Task as a Runnable, Not as a Thread
section:Spot the Problem: A Thread Subclass Handed to a Pool

aspects.says: A virtual thread is always a daemon, so virtual threads started from main hold nothing open at exit.
basis: section:A Virtual Thread Is Cheap to Create and to Block, Not Faster at Computing

aspects.says: One virtual thread per task makes many blocking tasks cheap, while CPU-bound tasks take the same time on either kind of thread.
basis: section:A Virtual Thread Is Cheap to Create and to Block, Not Faster at Computing
